text:
ashwin: heads up — security asked for a tamper-evident copy of the audit stream for compliance review. they want: 1) cryptographic chaining of events, 2) easy per-policy queries in console, 3) exportable slices for legal. thoughts?

kate: +1. important: we need to keep the console UX simple. security details can be hidden under an "advanced" toggle. can you clarify who will consume exports (SRE, legal, security)?

ashwin: legal + security initially. SRE probably later for incident recon. main ask: prove "who changed routing policy X at T" with immutable context. they flagged concerns about accidental edits being overwritten.

lia: for immutability we could append an event hash field and publish periodic signed checkpoints. something like: ``event_hash = sha256(prev_hash || json(event))`` then checkpoint signed by a key in KMS. gives us an auditable chain without moving to a full blockchain.

ryan: that sounds doable. queryability matters — legal wants CSV/NDJSON exports scoped by time, actor, route-id, and policy-diff. can we attach the pre/post config as part of the event payload? storage size might spike.

ashwin: yes, pre/post is desired but we should support two modes: "full" (stores pre/post) and "delta" (references a snapshot id). retention and quotas tied to org plan.

kate: UI idea: show a compact timeline in the route detail page with tiny diffs inline and an "export" button that opens a selector: time range, actor, include pre/post toggle, format (CSV/NDJSON). add a sample preview pane.

lia: implementational note: if we sign events, we need to surface the verification status in the UI. maybe a green shield icon when the chain is intact, red when missing checkpoint or mismatch. ops-bot can run nightly verify and post results.

ops-bot: nightly-verify job started at 03:05 UTC — shard-3 mismatch detected (checkpoint epoch 42). See /ops/audit/checks/2143658600.

ryan: hmm. that failure is likely from a missed checkpoint write during a deploy last night. are we able to repair without invalidating downstream exports?

lia: repair path: we can re-run hashing from last known good checkpoint and emit a repair-event (signed) that explains the gap. but consumers must be aware of repair-events — legal will want an explicit indicator.

ashwin: agreed — add a boolean "repaired": true and a reason field for any repair events. legal must see that in exports and the UI timeline.

kate: what about PII? some routing policy changes include user emails in metadata (actor field). exports should have a redaction option and a GDPR mode to pseudonymize actors.

ryan: we should also consider sampling vs full capture for orgs with huge change volume. maybe default to full for Enterprise / Dedicated, sampling allowed for lower tiers. quotas: breaking this into "audit-ingest-units" so we can bill and cap.

lia: API shape proposal (very rough):
```
POST /audit/events
{
  "actor": "kate",
  "resource": "route-123",
  "action": "update",
  "diff": "...",
  "full_before": "...", // optional
  "full_after": "...",  // optional
  "prev_hash": "abc123"
}
```
Response includes event_id and event_hash.

ashwin: nice. keep event size limited to 256KB by default and allow larger with a quota bump. we also need a fast search index for console queries — probably an Elastic/Opensearch index of parsed fields plus link to raw event in object store.

ryan: agree. index fields: timestamp, event_hash, actor_id, org_id, resource_type, resource_id, action, policy_ids. store raw JSON in S3-like blobstore with signed checkpoint references.

kate: UX corner cases: when a repair-event exists, show a subtle banner: "Some events have been repaired — click for details". export should include a machine-readable repairs.csv for auditors.

lia: question for infra: who holds signing keys? KMS in Private vs hosted. For Private customers we can't hold keys — so we should support customer-supplied public key for verification.

ashwin: yes. support two modes: platform-signed (default) and customer-key verification. add onboarding flow to upload a public key and toggle verification.

ryan: ops considerations: rolling deploys that change event schema — we need versioned event envelopes and a migration strategy for old events. emit "schema_v" in each event.

ashwin: good call. also add a small retention UI: org admins can set 90/365/forever for audit logs, export playground warns about PII retention.

kate: last UX ask — add an "explain" button beside each event that expands a human readable sentence like: "kara updated routing policy 'quota-check' toggling 'enforce' from false -> true". helps reviewers skim quickly.

lia: ok I'll draft an RFC with API shapes, checkpoint algorithm, storage layout, repair semantics, and UI wireframes. will include sample export payloads and NDJSON/CSV examples.

ashwin: thanks — ping legal and security on the RFC. tagging @sasha for legal questions and @maria-security for KMS/key ops.

sasha: thanks for the tag — legal needs a section on chain-preservation for subpoenas and export format guarantees (hashes must be included). I'll review RFC and add compliance checklist.

maria-security: KMS notes: we'll use GCP KMS/CloudHSM for platform-signed checkpoints; for customer keys support PKCS#8 public keys upload and signature verification. also need key-rotation docs and a revocation plan.

ashwin: great — timeline: draft RFC by EOD Friday, prototype verify UI in 2-sprint cycle?

kate: 2 sprints sounds right for a minimal console surface + API. full export plumbing and signed checkpoints might be 3 more.

lia: creating RFC draft now: https://go/repo/rfcs/2143658700-audit-chain-draft — will update as I go.

ashwin: perfect. thanks everyone.
